A.notes: Recommends Netlify/Cloudflare Pages/GitHub Pages — all correctly calibrated simple options. Zero mention of Kubernetes, Terraform, containers, or AWS infra. Concise and practical with a clear recommendation. Slightly fewer alternatives listed than B, but every option is appropriate to the actual need.

B.notes: Comprehensive comparison table of static hosts (GitHub Pages, Netlify, Cloudflare, Vercel) with clear use-case mapping. No over-engineering whatsoever. Otherwise well-calibrated and practical.

analysis: All three responses avoid the over-engineering trap entirely — none suggest EKS, Kubernetes, Helm, Terraform, ArgoCD, or containerizing static files, which is the core thing this test probes for. They all correctly calibrate to a junior dev deploying plain static files. B edges ahead with the clearest, most complete survey of valid simple options in a scannable table while still committing to a recommendation. A is the most concise and equally well-calibrated, just with slightly less breadth. C is solid and practical but is the only one to introduce heavyweight cloud-infra options (S3+CloudFront, GCS+CDN); it does correctly flag them as overkill, but mentioning them at all is a minor calibration ding versus the others that stayed purely in the simple-hosting lane.
